unfold.unfolded: Let $S$ be an ordered semigroup and $m\ge 1$ an integer. An $m$-bi-interior ideal of $S$ is a non-empty subset $B$ with $(BS^mB]\cap(S^mBS^m]\subseteq B$ and $(B]=B$. Then the following hold. (1) Every $m$-left ideal and every $m$-right ideal of $S$ is an $m$-bi-interior ideal of $S$. (2) Every $m$-ideal of $S$ is an $m$-bi-interior ideal of $S$. (3) If $A$ and $B$ are $m$-bi-interior ideals of $S$ and $A\cap B\neq\emptyset$, then $A\cap B$ is an $m$-bi-interior ideal of $S$. (4) The intersection of an $m$-right ideal and an $m$-left ideal of $S$ is an $m$-bi-interior ideal of $S$. (5) Every $m$-quasi-ideal of $S$ is an $m$-bi-interior ideal of $S$. (6) Every $m$-bi-ideal of $S$ is an $m$-bi-interior ideal of $S$. (7) Every $m$-interior ideal of $S$ is an $m$-bi-interior ideal of $S$. (8) If $B$ is an $m$-bi-interior ideal of $S$, then $(BS]$ and $(SB]$ are $m$-bi-interior ideals of $S$. (9) If $T$ is an $m$-right ideal of $S$ and $B$ is an $m$-bi-interior ideal of $S$, then $B\cap T$ is an $m$-bi-interior ideal of $S$. Here an $m$-left ideal is a subsemigroup $L$ with $S^mL\subseteq L$ and $(L]=L$; an $m$-right ideal is a subsemigroup $R$ with $RS^m\subseteq R$ and $(R]=R$; an $m$-bi-ideal is a subsemigroup $B$ with $BS^mB\subseteq B$ and $(B]=B$; an $m$-interior ideal is a subsemigroup $I$ with $S^mIS^m\subseteq I$ and $(I]=I$; an $m$-quasi-ideal is a subsemigroup $Q$ with $(S^mQ]\cap(QS^m]\subseteq Q$ and $(Q]=Q$; and $(X]=\{x\in S : x\le y \text{ for some } y\in X\}$. The term $m$-ideal is used as background.
